claim: usp-50(xd413) mutation leads to greatly reduced lysosome size in C. elegans
source: In usp-50(xd413), a recessive mutation isolated from a genetic screen of worms mutagenized with EMS (ethylmethane sulfonate), lysosomes appear to be greatly reduced in size (Figure 1B and D).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy images (Figure 1B and D) showing reduced lysosome size in the mutant compared to wild-type, and quantification data presented in Figure 1D.

claim: usp-50(gk632973) animals show normal lysosome distribution during L4 stage but reduced lysosome size at adult stage
source: For another usp-50 allele, gk632973, the lysosome distribution and morphology appear normal during L4 stage (Figure 1C). However, when usp-50(gk632973) animals reach adult stage, the individual size and total volume of lysosomes are also reduced (Figure 1C and D).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy images (Figure 1C) and quantification data (Figure 1D) showing temporal differences in lysosome phenotypes.

claim: NUC-1 protein is properly targeted to LAAT-1-containing vesicles in usp-50(xd413) animals
source: In usp-50(xd413) animals, the NUC-1 protein is properly targeted to LAAT-1-containing vesicles (Figure 1E and F and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A), which indicates that the assembly of de novo lysosomes is not affected by usp-50.
evidence: The claim is supported by co-localization microscopy images (Figure 1E and F) and Pearson's correlation coefficient analysis (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).

claim: usp-50 encodes the C. elegans homolog of Saccharomyces cerevisiae Doa4p and human USP8/UBPY
source: usp-50 encodes the C. elegans homolog of Saccharomyces cerevisiae Doa4p and human USP8/UBPY (Bowers et al., 2004; Huynh et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Bowers et al., 2004; Huynh et al., 2016) that established the homology relationships.

claim: usp-50(xd413) mutation causes a G541A substitution in the UCH domain
source: The molecular lesions of both usp-50(xd413) and usp-50(gk632973) occur in the UCH domain, leading to a G541A and A523V substitution, respectively.
evidence: The claim states specific molecular lesions identified in the mutant alleles.

claim: usp-50(gk632973) mutation causes an A523V substitution in the UCH domain
source: The molecular lesions of both usp-50(xd413) and usp-50(gk632973) occur in the UCH domain, leading to a G541A and A523V substitution, respectively.
evidence: The claim states specific molecular lesions identified in the mutant alleles.

claim: The punctate HGRS-1::GFP signal is greatly reduced in usp-50 mutants
source: When usp-50 is mutated, the punctate HGRS-1::GFP and STAM-1 signals are greatly reduced (Figure 1G and H and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B), which is consistent with the role of USP8 in stabilizing the ESCRT-0 complex (Kato et al., 2000; Mizuno et al., 2006; Niendorf et al., 2007; Row et al., 2006; Zhang et al., 2014a).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy images (Figure 1G and H) and quantification data (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B), and is consistent with cited literature on USP8 function.

claim: The punctate STAM-1 signal is greatly reduced in usp-50 mutants
source: When usp-50 is mutated, the punctate HGRS-1::GFP and STAM-1 signals are greatly reduced (Figure 1G and H and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B), which is consistent with the role of USP8 in stabilizing the ESCRT-0 complex (Kato et al., 2000; Mizuno et al., 2006; Niendorf et al., 2007; Row et al., 2006; Zhang et al., 2014a).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy images (Figure 1G and H) showing reduced STAM-1 signal, consistent with cited literature.

claim: The size of individual early endosomes is significantly increased in usp-50 mutants
source: We found that the size of individual EEs is significantly increased (Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification data in Figure 2B showing increased individual vesicle size.

claim: The total volume of early endosomes in usp-50 mutants remains similar to wild-type
source: Meanwhile, the total volume of EEs in usp-50 mutants remains similar to wild-type (Figure 2B), implying that the homotypic fusion of EEs is probably increased.
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification data in Figure 2B showing no significant difference in total volume.

claim: The enlarged early endosomes in usp-50(xd413) are not coated with the lysosome marker LAAT-1::mCherry
source: The enlarged EEs in usp-50(xd413) are not coated with the lysosome marker LAAT-1::mCherry (Figure 2C and D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by co-localization microscopy images (Figure 2C and D) and Pearson's correlation coefficient analysis (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).

claim: The enlarged early endosome defect in usp-50(xd413) mutants is rescued by worm usp-50
source: The enlarged EE defect in usp-50(xd413) mutants is rescued by either worm usp-50 or human USP8 (Figure 2G and J and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B), which suggests that the function of USP-50/USP8 is evolutionarily conserved.
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy images (Figure 2G) and quantification data (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B) showing rescue of the phenotype.

claim: The enlarged early endosome defect in usp-50(xd413) mutants is rescued by human USP8
source: The enlarged EE defect in usp-50(xd413) mutants is rescued by either worm usp-50 or human USP8 (Figure 2G and J and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B), which suggests that the function of USP-50/USP8 is evolutionarily conserved.
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy images (Figure 2J) and quantification data (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B) showing rescue of the phenotype.

claim: The function of USP-50/USP8 is evolutionarily conserved
source: The enlarged EE defect in usp-50(xd413) mutants is rescued by either worm usp-50 or human USP8 (Figure 2G and J and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B), which suggests that the function of USP-50/USP8 is evolutionarily conserved.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the rescue experiments showing that human USP8 can functionally replace worm usp-50.

claim: USP8 depletion causes early endosome enlargement in human breast cancer SUM159 cells
source: Indeed, when we knocked out the expression of USP8 (USP8-KO) in human breast cancer SUM159 cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C), the transient expression of EGFP-2xFYVE confirmed that USP8 depletion caused EE enlargement (Figure 2K).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy images and quantification (Figure 2K) showing enlarged early endosomes in USP8-KO cells.

claim: Many abnormal large vesicles with various intraluminal contents are detected in usp-50(xd413) mutants by transmission electron microscopy
source: Compared to wild-type, many abnormal large vesicles with various intraluminal contents were detected in usp-50(xd413) mutants (Figure 2M–Q).
evidence: The claim is supported by transmission electron microscopy images (Figure 2M–Q) showing abnormal vesicles.

claim: About 58.7% of abnormal vesicles in usp-50(xd413) mutants contain abundant intraluminal vesicle structures
source: The first class is composed of vesicles containing abundant intraluminal vesicle structures (Figure 2N). About 58.7% of the abnormal vesicles belong to this category.
evidence: The claim is supported by electron microscopy analysis and quantification of vesicle types.

claim: About 26.8% of abnormal vesicles in usp-50(xd413) mutants are filled with threadlike membrane structures
source: The second class (26.8%) includes vesicles filled with threadlike membrane structures (Figure 2Q).
evidence: The claim is supported by electron microscopy analysis and quantification of vesicle types.

claim: About 22.4% of abnormal vesicles in usp-50(xd413) mutants are loaded with threadlike membrane structures and electron-dense material
source: Vesicles of the third type (22.4%) are loaded with threadlike membrane structures and electron-dense material (Figure 2P).
evidence: The claim is supported by electron microscopy analysis and quantification of vesicle types.

claim: About 4.9% of abnormal vesicles in usp-50(xd413) mutants contain various cellular organelles including mitochondria
source: The fourth class, which accounts for a relatively small proportion of mutant vesicles (4.9%), contains various cellular organelles, for instance mitochondria (Figure 2Q).
evidence: The claim is supported by electron microscopy analysis and quantification of vesicle types.

claim: GFP-tagged USP-50 protein is co-localized with mCherry::RAB-5 in worm epidermal cells
source: In worm epidermal cells, the GFP-tagged USP-50 protein is co-localized with mCherry::RAB-5 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A) but not with mCherry::RAB-7 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B), consistent with the early endosomal localization of USP-50/USP8 (Mizuno et al., 2005; Row et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by co-localization microscopy images (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).

claim: GFP-tagged USP-50 protein is not co-localized with mCherry::RAB-7 in worm epidermal cells
source: In worm epidermal cells, the GFP-tagged USP-50 protein is co-localized with mCherry::RAB-5 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A) but not with mCherry::RAB-7 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B), consistent with the early endosomal localization of USP-50/USP8 (Mizuno et al., 2005; Row et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by co-localization microscopy images (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).

claim: The early endosome localization of USP-50 is not dependent on its deubiquitination activity
source: When we mutated C492 to Alanine, we found that the GFP-tagged USP-50(C492A) protein is still co-localized with mCherry::RAB-5 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C). Thus, the EE localization of USP-50 is not dependent on its deubiquitination activity.
evidence: The claim is supported by co-localization microscopy images (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C) showing that the catalytically inactive mutant still localizes to early endosomes.

claim: The C492A mutation has a dominant-negative effect on USP-50 function
source: Meanwhile, the mCherry::RAB-5 signal is strongly enhanced by the overexpression of USP-50(C492A) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C), suggesting that the C492A mutation may have a dominant-negative effect on USP-50 function.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that overexpression of the catalytically inactive mutant enhances RAB-5 signal, suggesting it interferes with normal USP-50 function.

claim: USP8-mEGFP co-localizes well with the early endosome marker mScarlet-I-EEA1
source: As shown in Figure 3, USP8-mEGFP co-localizes well with the EE marker mScarlet-I-EEA1 (Figure 3A).
evidence: The claim is supported by co-localization microscopy images (Figure 3A).

claim: Late endosome or lysosome markers have little overlap with the USP8-mEGFP signal
source: In contrast, LE or lysosome markers, including mScarlet-I-Rab7a and Lamp1-mScarlet-I, have little overlap with the USP8-mEGFP signal (Figure 3B and C).
evidence: The claim is supported by co-localization microscopy images (Figure 3B and C) showing minimal overlap.

claim: USP8-mEGFP forms individual spots located on one side of enlarged endosomes caused by Rab5c-Q80L overexpression
source: Constitutively activated Rab5 GTPase (Rab5c-Q80L) causes enlarged EEs (Stenmark et al., 1994; Wegner et al., 2010). Instead of being evenly distributed, USP8-mEGFP formed individual spots located on one side of the enlarged endosomes (Figure 3D).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy images (Figure 3D) showing the asymmetric distribution of USP8 on enlarged endosomes.

claim: USP8-mEGFP dots are located at subdomains of early endosomes as shown by structured illumination microscopy
source: We further analyzed the sub-organelle distribution of USP8 using structured illumination microscopy (SIM). Consistent with what we observed in enlarged EEs caused by Rab5c-Q80L overexpression, the USP8-mEGFP dots indeed located at subdomains of EEs (Figure 3E).
evidence: The claim is supported by structured illumination microscopy images (Figure 3E) showing sub-organelle localization.

claim: USP8-mEGFP is recruited to nascent mScarlet-I-Rab5c-positive vesicles
source: We found that USP8-mEGFP was recruited to these nascent mScarlet-I-Rab5c-positive vesicles which appeared around the bottom surface of the cells (Figure 3F).
evidence: The claim is supported by time-lapse microscopy images (Figure 3F) showing dynamic recruitment.

claim: USP-50 can bind to RABX-5
source: By searching the putative USP-50-binding partners, we found that USP-50 can bind to RABX-5, the worm homolog of Rabex5 protein (Figure 4A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation experiments (Figure 4A and B).

claim: The C-terminal coiled-coil and C-terminal proline-rich domains of RABX-5 are sufficient for interaction with USP-50
source: In general, the C-terminal coiled-coil (CC) and the C-terminal proline-rich (PR) domains are sufficient for RABX-5 to interact with USP-50.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoprecipitation tests with truncation mutants (Figure 4D).

claim: The N-terminal region of RABX-5 including A20-zinc finger domain, motif interacting with ubiquitin, membrane-binding motif, and helical bundle domain can mediate USP-50 binding
source: Meanwhile, the N-terminal region, including an A20-zinc finger domain (ZF), a motif interacting with ubiquitin (U), the membrane-binding motif (MB), and the downstream helical bundle domain (HB) of RABX-5 could also mediate USP-50 binding.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoprecipitation tests with truncation mutants (Figure 4D).

claim: Including the Vps9 domain enhances the molecular interaction between RABX-5 and USP-50
source: Further including Vps9 domain enhances the molecular interaction between RABX-5 and USP-50 (Figure 4C and D).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoprecipitation tests (Figure 4D) showing enhanced binding with Vps9 domain inclusion.

claim: rabx-5 is required for the endosomal localization of USP-50
source: In rabx-5(null) mutant animals, the punctate USP-50::GFP signal becomes diffusely distributed (Figure 4F and G). Thus, rabx-5 is required for the endosomal localization of USP-50.
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy images (Figure 4F and G) showing loss of punctate USP-50 localization in rabx-5(null) mutants.

claim: Early endosomes labeled with 2xFYVE are indistinguishable from wild-type in rabx-5(null) mutant animals
source: In rabx-5(null) mutant animals, EEs labeled with 2xFYVE are indistinguishable from those in wild-type controls (Figure 4H and I).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy images and quantification (Figure 4H and I).

claim: rabx-5(null) mutation suppresses the enlarged early endosome phenotype of usp-50(xd413)
source: Furthermore, when rabx-5(null) was introduced into usp-50(xd413) mutant backgrounds, the enlarged EE phenotype of usp-50(xd413) was efficiently suppressed (Figure 4H and I).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy images and quantification (Figure 4H and I) showing suppression of the phenotype.

claim: USP-50 likely exerts its regulatory effects on early endosome size through RABX-5
source: These findings suggest that USP-50 likely exerts its regulatory effects on EE size through RABX-5.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the genetic suppression experiments showing that loss of rabx-5 suppresses the usp-50 phenotype.

claim: The RABX-5::GFP KI signal is greatly enhanced in usp-50 mutants
source: In wild-type animals, the fluorescence signal of RABX-5::GFP in hyp7 is rather dim (Figure 5A). When usp-50 is mutated, the RABX-5::GFP KI signal is greatly enhanced (Figure 5B).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy images (Figure 5A and B) showing enhanced RABX-5 signal in mutants.

claim: USP8-KO causes a significant increase in the number of enlarged endosomes in Rabex5-mEGFP+/+ SUM159 cells
source: USP8-KO also caused a significant increase in the number of enlarged endosomes in Rabex5-mEGFP+/+ SUM159 cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A–C and E).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy images and quantification (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A–C and E).

claim: Rabex5-mEGFP signals are enriched and co-localized well with the mScarlet-I-Rab5c signal on enlarged endosomes
source: Rabex5-mEGFP signals were enriched and co-localized well with the mScarlet-I-Rab5c signal on the enlarged endosomes (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by co-localization microscopy images (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).

claim: The enlarged early endosomes in USP8-KO cells are coated with both Rabex5 and EEA1
source: Antibody staining of endogenous EEA1 further showed that the enlarged EEs in USP8-KO cells were coated with both Rabex5 and EEA1 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence microscopy images (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).

claim: GFP::RAB-5 KI-labeled vesicles are significantly enlarged in usp-50 mutants
source: Indeed, in usp-50 mutants, the GFP::RAB-5 KI-labeled vesicles are significantly enlarged (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A–C) and the proportion of membrane-associated GFP::RAB-5 KI is also increased (Figure 5—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy images and quantification (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A–C).

claim: The proportion of membrane-associated GFP::RAB-5 KI is increased in usp-50 mutants
source: Indeed, in usp-50 mutants, the GFP::RAB-5 KI-labeled vesicles are significantly enlarged (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A–C) and the proportion of membrane-associated GFP::RAB-5 KI is also increased (Figure 5—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification data (Figure 5—figure supplement 2D).

claim: Loss of usp-50 leads to more activated RAB-5 in vivo
source: We utilized EEA1-NT (Figure 5—figure supplement 2E) to show that loss of usp-50 indeed led to more activated RAB-5 in vivo (Figure 5—figure supplement 2F).
evidence: The claim is supported by pull-down assays (Figure 5—figure supplement 2F) using the RAB-5 effector EEA1-NT.

claim: The total RAB-5 protein level is increased by usp-50 mutation
source: In addition, the total RAB-5 protein level is increased by usp-50 mutation (Figure 5—figure supplement 2G and H), which implies that RAB-5 activation may stabilize RAB-5 protein.
evidence: The claim is supported by western blot analysis and quantification (Figure 5—figure supplement 2G and H).

claim: Early endosomes labeled by Rab5 are significantly enlarged in USP8-KD SUM159 cells
source: To explore the relationship between Rab5 and USP8 in SUM159 cells, we knocked down the expression of USP8 by siRNA (USP8-KD) in the clonal genome-edited EGFP-Rab5c+/+ cells. We found that EEs, labeled by Rab5, are significantly enlarged (Figure 5—figure supplement 2I and J).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy images and quantification (Figure 5—figure supplement 2I and J).

claim: USP-50/USP8 recruitment dissociates RABX-5 from endosomes
source: Taken together, these results indicate that USP-50/USP8 recruitment dissociates RABX-5 from endosomes, and subsequently diminish Rab5 signaling.
evidence: The claim is inferred from multiple lines of evidence showing enhanced RABX-5 signal and increased Rab5 activity in usp-50 mutants.

claim: The enzyme-inactive USP-50(C492A) cannot rescue the enhanced endosomal RABX-5 signal in usp-50 mutant animals
source: The enzyme-inactive USP-50(C492A) cannot rescue the enhanced endosomal RABX-5 signal in usp-50 mutant animals (Figure 5C and D).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy images (Figure 5C and D) showing lack of rescue by the catalytically inactive mutant.

claim: USP-50 acts through its deubiquitination activity to dissociate RABX-5 from endosomes
source: This suggests that USP-50 acts through its deubiquitination activity to dissociate RABX-5 from endosomes.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that the catalytically inactive mutant cannot rescue the phenotype.

claim: The K88 and K323 residues of RABX-5 are modified by ubiquitin in vivo
source: We found that the K88 and K323 residues of RABX-5 are modified by ubiquitin in vivo (Figure 5—figure supplement 3A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by ubiquitination proteomics analysis (Figure 5—figure supplement 3A and B).

claim: K88 is located in the membrane-binding motif of RABX-5
source: K88 is located in the membrane-binding motif, while K323 resides in the conserved Vps9 domain of RABX-5 (Figure 5—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: The claim is supported by the domain structure diagram (Figure 5—figure supplement 3B).

claim: K323 resides in the conserved Vps9 domain of RABX-5
source: K88 is located in the membrane-binding motif, while K323 resides in the conserved Vps9 domain of RABX-5 (Figure 5—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: The claim is supported by the domain structure diagram (Figure 5—figure supplement 3B).

claim: The RABX-5(K88R)::GFP KI signal is greatly enhanced in usp-50 mutants
source: When usp-50 is mutated, the RABX-5(K88R)::GFP KI signal is greatly enhanced and displays an apparent punctate pattern (Figure 5F and I), which is similar to what we observed with the wild-type RABX-5::GFP KI line.
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy images and line scan analysis (Figure 5F and I).

claim: The signal from RABX-5(K323A)::GFP KI remains dim in both wild-type and usp-50 mutant animals
source: In contrast, when K323 is mutated, the signal from RABX-5(K323A)::GFP KI remains dim in both wild-type and usp-50 mutant animals (Figure 5G–I).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy images and line scan analysis (Figure 5G–I).

claim: USP-50 cannot regulate the endosomal localization of RABX-5 when K323 is mutated
source: These observations suggest that USP-50 cannot regulate the endosomal localization of RABX-5 when K323 is mutated.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that K323R mutation prevents the enhancement of RABX-5 signal in usp-50 mutants.

claim: The rabx-5(K323R) mutation suppresses both the enlarged early endosome and diminished late endosome phenotypes of usp-50
source: Furthermore, the rabx-5(K323R) mutation successfully suppressed both the enlarged EE and diminished LE phenotypes of usp-50 (Figure 5J–M).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy images and quantification (Figure 5J–M) showing suppression of both phenotypes.

claim: USP-50 recruitment to early endosomes relies on RABX-5
source: Taken together, USP-50 recruitment to EEs relies on RABX-5, and through its deubiquitination action on the Vps9 domain of RABX-5, USP-50 dissociates RABX-5 from EEs, thereby terminating Rab5 signaling to promote endosome maturation.
evidence: The claim is supported by the observation that USP-50 localization is lost in rabx-5(null) mutants.

claim: Through its deubiquitination action on the Vps9 domain of RABX-5, USP-50 dissociates RABX-5 from early endosomes
source: Taken together, USP-50 recruitment to EEs relies on RABX-5, and through its deubiquitination action on the Vps9 domain of RABX-5, USP-50 dissociates RABX-5 from EEs, thereby terminating Rab5 signaling to promote endosome maturation.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the K323R mutation experiments showing that this ubiquitination site is critical for USP-50 function.

claim: The GFP::SAND-1 puncta are diminished in rabx-5(null) mutants
source: In the absence of RABX-5 (rabx-5 null), the GFP::SAND-1 puncta are diminished (Figure 6A, B, and D) and the LAAT-1::GFP-labeled lysosome structures are also reduced (Figure 6E and F and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy images and line scan analysis (Figure 6A, B, and D).

claim: The LAAT-1::GFP-labeled lysosome structures are reduced in rabx-5(null) mutants
source: In the absence of RABX-5 (rabx-5 null), the GFP::SAND-1 puncta are diminished (Figure 6A, B, and D) and the LAAT-1::GFP-labeled lysosome structures are also reduced (Figure 6E and F and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy images and quantification (Figure 6E and F and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).

claim: The punctate distribution of GFP::SAND-1 is lost in usp-50 mutants
source: Intriguingly, when we introduced the GFP::SAND-1 marker into usp-50 mutants, we found that the punctate distribution of GFP::SAND-1 is lost (Figure 6A, C, and D).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy images and line scan analysis (Figure 6A, C, and D).

claim: mEGFP-tagged endogenous Mon1a is localized on both Rab5-positive early endosomes and Rab7-positive late endosomes
source: In SUM159 cells, mEGFP-tagged endogenous Mon1a (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B) is localized on both Rab5-positive EEs and Rab7-positive LEs (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C and D).
evidence: The claim is supported by co-localization microscopy images (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C and D).

claim: Endogenous Mon1b is more localized on late endosomes
source: In contrast, endogenous Mon1b (Figure 6—figure supplement 1E) is more localized on LEs (Figure 6—figure supplement 1F and G).
evidence: The claim is supported by co-localization microscopy images (Figure 6—figure supplement 1F and G).

claim: The number of vesicles positive for mEGFP-Mon1a is greatly reduced when USP8 expression is knocked down
source: When the expression of USP8 in the mEGFP-Mon1a+/+ or mEGFP-Mon1b+/+ cells was knocked down by siRNA, we found that the number of vesicles positive for mEGFP-Mon1a or mEGFP-Mon1b was greatly reduced (Figure 6H and I).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy images and quantification (Figure 6H).

claim: The number of vesicles positive for mEGFP-Mon1b is greatly reduced when USP8 expression is knocked down
source: When the expression of USP8 in the mEGFP-Mon1a+/+ or mEGFP-Mon1b+/+ cells was knocked down by siRNA, we found that the number of vesicles positive for mEGFP-Mon1a or mEGFP-Mon1b was greatly reduced (Figure 6H and I).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy images and quantification (Figure 6I).

claim: The function of USP8/USP-50 in endosomal localization of SAND-1/Mon1-Ccz1 is evolutionarily conserved
source: Taken together, these results indicate that the function of USP8/USP-50 in endosomal localization of SAND-1/Mon1-Ccz1 is evolutionarily conserved.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the similar effects of USP8/USP-50 loss on Mon1/SAND-1 localization in both worms and mammalian cells.

claim: Early endosomes are enlarged in sand-1 mutants
source: We noticed that when sand-1 is mutated, the EEs are enlarged (Figure 6J–L and Figure 6—figure supplement 1H) and LEs/lysosomes become smaller (Figure 6M–O and Figure 6—figure supplement 1I), which is highly similar to usp-50 mutants.
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy images and quantification (Figure 6J–L and Figure 6—figure supplement 1H).

claim: Late endosomes/lysosomes become smaller in sand-1 mutants
source: We noticed that when sand-1 is mutated, the EEs are enlarged (Figure 6J–L and Figure 6—figure supplement 1H) and LEs/lysosomes become smaller (Figure 6M–O and Figure 6—figure supplement 1I), which is highly similar to usp-50 mutants.
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy images and quantification (Figure 6M–O and Figure 6—figure supplement 1I).

claim: The USP-50 protein is able to bind to SAND-1
source: Furthermore, Co-IP (co-immunoprecipitation) experiments indicated that the USP-50 protein is able to bind to SAND-1 (Figure 6P), which is consistent with the role of USP-50 in endosomal localization of SAND-1.
evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation experiments (Figure 6P).

claim: The punctate RAB-7 signal is greatly reduced by loss of function of sand-1
source: Indeed, with the GFP::RAB-7 KI line, we found that the punctate RAB-7 signal was greatly reduced by loss of function of sand-1 (Figure 6Q and R).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy images and line scan analysis (Figure 6Q and R).

claim: The punctate GFP::RAB-7 KI signal is reduced in usp-50 mutants
source: In usp-50 mutants, the punctate GFP::RAB-7 KI signal is also reduced (Figure 6S and T).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy images and line scan analysis (Figure 6S and T).

claim: Overexpression of wild-type rab-7 greatly suppresses the early endosome enlargement phenotype of usp-50 mutants
source: Therefore, we overexpressed the wild-type rab-7 gene and found that the EE enlargement phenotype of usp-50 mutants was greatly suppressed (Figure 6U–X).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy images and quantification (Figure 6U–X) showing suppression of the phenotype.

claim: The recruitment of USP-50/USP8, dependent on Rabex5, dissociates Rabex5 from early endosomes
source: In conclusion, we propose that the recruitment of USP-50/USP8, dependent on Rabex5, dissociates Rabex5 from EEs. Concurrently, this recruitment promotes the enrollment of SAND-1/Mon1-Ccz1, thereby facilitating the maturation of endosomes (Figure 6Y).
evidence: The claim is a summary of the working model supported by multiple lines of experimental evidence presented in the study.

claim: The recruitment of USP-50/USP8 promotes the enrollment of SAND-1/Mon1-Ccz1
source: In conclusion, we propose that the recruitment of USP-50/USP8, dependent on Rabex5, dissociates Rabex5 from EEs. Concurrently, this recruitment promotes the enrollment of SAND-1/Mon1-Ccz1, thereby facilitating the maturation of endosomes (Figure 6Y).
evidence: The claim is a summary of the working model supported by multiple lines of experimental evidence presented in the study.

claim: The recruitment of USP-50/USP8 facilitates the maturation of endosomes
source: In conclusion, we propose that the recruitment of USP-50/USP8, dependent on Rabex5, dissociates Rabex5 from EEs. Concurrently, this recruitment promotes the enrollment of SAND-1/Mon1-Ccz1, thereby facilitating the maturation of endosomes (Figure 6Y).
evidence: The claim is a summary of the working model supported by multiple lines of experimental evidence presented in the study.

claim: USP8 is important for the stability and ubiquitination status of various ESCRT components
source: USP8 is important for the stability and ubiquitination status of various ESCRT components (Adoro et al., 2017; Crespo-Yàñez et al., 2018; Mathieu et al., 2022; Mizuno et al., 2006; Niendorf et al., 2007; Zhang et al., 2014a).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to multiple previous studies.

claim: A large number of abnormal vesicular structures accumulate in usp-50 mutants
